title: Ones and Zeroes
summary: Given an array of binary strings and two integers m and n, determine the size of the largest subset of these strings such that the subset contains no more than m zeros and no more than n ones in total.
statement: Given an array of binary strings and two integers m and n, determine the size of the largest subset of these strings such that the subset contains no more than m zeros and no more than n ones in total.
constraints: 1 <= strs.length <= 600; each binary string has length 1..100; 1 <= m,n <= 100.
Select the maximum number of array entries using at most m zeros AND at most n ones in total.
Each index can be chosen once. Repeated equal strings at different indices are separate choices. Budgets need not be used exactly.
hints: Each string costs two resources and contributes one selected item.
Use a table indexed by available zeros and ones, storing the maximum item count.
For each string cost (z,o), update both capacity loops backward with 1+dp[zeros-z][ones-o].
Backward updates read the previous item layer, including strings with zero cost in one resource. Do not deduplicate entries.
editorial: For each entry the optimum either skips it or takes it from a state with both resource costs removed. Descending capacities implement this 0/1 choice without reusing the same entry. Repeated strings remain separate items. The oracle enumerates index subsets and counts their literal zeros and ones.

tests.explanation: Choose 10,0001,1,0: four entries consume five zeros and three ones. The 111001 entry alone has too many ones.
All three indices fit. The two identical zero strings are distinct available entries, not one reusable item.
